chapter: Chicago clubs, entertainers and tent shows
title: Singing bandleaders: Armstrong, Al Williams and backup singers
summary: Louis was the first singing star; Al Williams sang with Wooding on records, and Earl Hines players did backup singing.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Right. Now what about male singers singing with the bands. Today, most -- well a lot of instrumentalists who also sing, they don't take that side of it seriously, but they'll sing anyway.
And I know, for instance, on some of the old Jimmy Noon records, where Junie C. Cobb would do a vocal or something.
Was Louie the first singing star of the --
I think he was, oh yes he was. Al Williams did some singing too. New Orleans type singing. Yes he did.
Yes, he did some singing with Sam Woodings band on some of the records that we did.
Uh-huh. And of course, Earl Hines and Money Cara --
-- and people were doing some little back-up singing there.
